aesop-apothecary.name: Aesop apothecary minimal still life
aesop-apothecary.oneLine: Stone, concrete, raw plaster, or linen substrate.
aesop-apothecary.notForUseWhen: Mass-market product, anything loud, family CPG.

apple-clean-studio.name: Apple-clean studio product
apple-clean-studio.oneLine: Pure white or pure black seamless backdrop, no horizon line.
apple-clean-studio.notForUseWhen: Lifestyle storytelling, editorial, anything needing context or mood.

archival-found-photo.name: Archival found-photograph treatment
archival-found-photo.oneLine: Period-correct degradation: faded color, slight yellowing, edge wear.
archival-found-photo.notForUseWhen: Modern tech, restrained luxury, anything aspirational-future.

ascii-art-portrait.name: ASCII-art portrait (text-as-image)
ascii-art-portrait.oneLine: Photo rendered entirely from **ASCII characters** (or extended ANSI character set) — text-as-image. Dark areas use dense characters (`@`, `#`, `M`), midtones use medium-density (`+`, `=`, `*`), highlights use sparse (`.`, ` `). Monospace, high-contrast. Used for tech / dev-tools marketing, terminal-on-web hero images, hacker-culture editorial, retro-BBS revival.

atkinson-dither-mac-classic.name: Atkinson dither (original-Macintosh classic)
atkinson-dither-mac-classic.oneLine: Photo reduced to **1-bit using Bill Atkinson's dithering algorithm** — created for the original Macintosh in 1984. Distinct from Bayer (regular grid) in that Atkinson is **error-diffusion** but only spreads ¾ of the quantization error (vs Floyd-Steinberg's full error), producing **stronger contrast, blown-out highlights, lots of white space**. The hallmark of early Macintosh screenshots, HyperCard stacks, MacPaint compositions. Bolder and cleaner than Bayer or Floyd-Steinberg.

backstage-fashion.name: Backstage editorial BTS
backstage-fashion.oneLine: Available light, sometimes mixed with hair-light or makeup-station tungsten.

bayer-dither-retro.name: Bayer-matrix ordered dither (retro 1-bit)
bayer-dither-retro.oneLine: Photo reduced to **1-bit** (or limited palette) using a **Bayer-matrix ordered-dithering algorithm** — produces a regular ordered-grid dotted pattern that looks like classic Game Boy / Macintosh / PC-98 era graphics. Distinct from halftone (which is luminance-modulated DOT SIZE) — Bayer is REGULAR-GRID threshold, dots are uniform in size, the PATTERN density is what changes per luminance zone. Also distinct from Atkinson dither (which is error-diffusion, irregular).

blade-runner-2049-monochrome-sections.name: Blade Runner 2049 monochrome-sections (Deakins)
blade-runner-2049-monochrome-sections.oneLine: Denis Villeneuve's *Blade Runner 2049* (2017), shot by **Roger Deakins** (Oscar for this film). The signature is the **single-chromatic monochromatic sections** — entire sequences bathed in ONE color (Las Vegas in **deep amber-orange/Martian red**, Niander Wallace's lair in **yellow**, the LAPD orphanage in **blue-grey**, the seawall in **green-grey**). Deakins built **custom Tiffen amber filters** for the Vegas sequences. Soft halogen-like light replaces the original 1982 film's hard noir shadows — there is *"no binary division of light and dark; everyone exists on a continuous spectrum between reality and artificiality."*
blade-runner-2049-monochrome-sections.notForUseWhen: cottagecore, kids brands, warm-lifestyle, positivity-kawaii, restrained-warm-editorial

bon-appetit-food.name: Bon Appétit moody food overhead
bon-appetit-food.oneLine: Dark wood, slate, or aged copper substrate.
bon-appetit-food.notForUseWhen: Fast casual, fast food, packaging hero shot, kid food.

bowie-rock-glamour.name: Rock-glamour stage editorial
bowie-rock-glamour.oneLine: Stage lighting recreated in studio: hot rim from behind, single colored gel.

cereal-lifestyle.name: Cereal magazine slow-travel lifestyle
cereal-lifestyle.oneLine: Cool muted palette, slight blue-gray cast.
cereal-lifestyle.notForUseWhen: Tech B2B, fast-paced consumer, anything kinetic.

chrome-hearts-editorial.name: Chrome Hearts night-glam editorial
chrome-hearts-editorial.oneLine: Heavy on-camera flash on goth-luxe subjects, leather and chrome jewelry catching highlights.

cinematic-street-anamorphic.name: Cinematic anamorphic street
cinematic-street-anamorphic.oneLine: Anamorphic 2.39:1 wide aspect, oval bokeh, blue horizontal lens flares.

circuit-bent-glitch.name: Circuit-bent glitch photo effect
circuit-bent-glitch.notForUseWhen: Premium, B2B, anything restrained or sincere.

clean-tech-lifestyle.name: Clean tech-lifestyle hero
clean-tech-lifestyle.oneLine: Subject mid-action with the product, natural ambient light.
clean-tech-lifestyle.notForUseWhen: Editorial mood, fast fashion, anything kinetic.

cos-lookbook.name: COS lookbook clean editorial
cos-lookbook.oneLine: Plaster wall or seamless paper backdrop, neutral palette.
cos-lookbook.notForUseWhen: Loud or kinetic brand, fast e-comm with high SKU count.

databend-jpeg-corrupt.name: Databend / JPEG-corruption glitch
databend-jpeg-corrupt.oneLine: Photo file corrupted at the **bytestream / file-format level** — JPEG block artifacts smeared into impossible geometry, PNG line-corruption causing horizontal channel-shifts, half-loaded image frames with chunks of green/magenta error-color. Distinct from `circuit-bent-glitch` (which is POST-PROCESSED stylised glitch art) — databending is FILE-FORMAT corruption that yields CHAOTIC ACCIDENTAL geometry that no human would design. The randomness is the point.

dreamy-haze.name: Dreamy soft haze portrait
dreamy-haze.oneLine: Diffusion filter or smoke, soft halation around all highlights.
dreamy-haze.notForUseWhen: Hardware product, B2B, anything needing clarity and detail.

eighties-cocaine-glam.name: 1980s cocaine-glam editorial
eighties-cocaine-glam.oneLine: Hard rim light from behind, soft fill from front.

euphoria-glitter-neon.name: Euphoria glitter-neon emotional-realism (Rév)
euphoria-glitter-neon.oneLine: HBO's *Euphoria* (created by Sam Levinson, shot by **Marcell Rév**) — the show that **invented the 2020s neon-glitter visual vocabulary**. The signature is **emotional realism** (Levinson's term) — the show looks like teenagers IMAGINE their lives to be, not based on documentary realism. Highly saturated pigment makeup (Doniella Davy) survives under Rév's dark colored lighting because the soft shades kept getting lost — **neons weren't a style choice; they were a problem-solving decision that became a global trend.**

face-id-dot-projector.name: Face-ID dot-projector / structured-light depth scan
face-id-dot-projector.oneLine: Subject's face (or object) mapped with the Apple-TrueDepth / Face-ID dot-projector pattern — **30,000+ infrared dots** projected onto the surface in a structured grid, the dots distorting along the contours of the face to reveal its 3D shape. Sci-fi / biometric / surveillance / AI-identity register. The dots themselves luminous against deep-shadow skin. Distinct from glitch art — this is BIOMETRIC SCAN, not corruption; the technology is real and the aesthetic emerges from that physical apparatus.
face-id-dot-projector.notForUseWhen: warm-lifestyle, cottagecore, kids brands, restrained editorial

fallen-angels-wide-angle-neon.name: Fallen Angels wide-angle neon-distortion (Doyle)
fallen-angels-wide-angle-neon.oneLine: Wong Kar-Wai's *Fallen Angels* (1995, *堕落天使*), shot by **Christopher Doyle** — the most extreme expression of the Wong/Doyle wide-angle handheld neon-soaked Hong Kong nightscape vocabulary. Doyle famously **started with a 9.8mm lens** and Wong Kar-Wai said *"let's go further"* — they ended up at **6.8mm**, an ultra-ultrawide that distorts the entire frame. The result: subjects are **simultaneously intimate (the camera is millimeters from their face) and alienated (the wide-angle distortion bends the space around them).**

florida-project-candy-anamorphic.name: Florida Project candy-anamorphic (Zabe)
florida-project-candy-anamorphic.oneLine: Sean Baker's *The Florida Project* (2017), shot by **Alexis Zabe** on **anamorphic 35mm film with Panavision Millennium XL2 + vintage E-series lenses**. The signature is the **already-candy-colored Florida** (purple motel, orange domes, mint pastels — found in the real-world location, not painted) photographed with the colors **"popped by just a degree"** to suggest a child's heightened sensory perception. Baker's rule: *"when I think of childhood, colors seem more vibrant — just enhance everything by a hair, but not hyper-real."*

genz-flash-disposable.name: Gen-Z disposable-camera flash editorial
genz-flash-disposable.oneLine: Hard on-camera flash, often at a party or backstage, slight red-eye risk.
genz-flash-disposable.notForUseWhen: Luxury, B2B, anything sincere, anything elderly-targeted.

gilden-flash-street.name: Bruce Gilden flash street portrait
gilden-flash-street.oneLine: 28mm wide lens, flash off-camera held in left hand, very close to subject's face.

golden-hour-indoor-warm.name: Golden-hour indoor warm (rays through window)
golden-hour-indoor-warm.oneLine: Late-afternoon (or early-morning) sun streaming **through a window into a domestic interior** — bedroom, kitchen, living room, gallery, studio. Strong directional warm-yellow rays cast visible streaks across the floor or wall. Subject lit from one side with a golden rim-light, deep warm-shadow on the opposite side. **Distinct from `photo-warm-minimal-daylight`** (which is overcast or open-door — no directional sun rays) — this one is the SPECIFIC magic moment of sunset hitting an interior space. Domestic / intimate / nostalgic / verging-on-melancholy register.
golden-hour-indoor-warm.notForUseWhen: fast e-comm, edgy fashion volume, B2B, kinetic-tech, restrained-clean tech marketing

goldin-diary.name: Nan Goldin diary flash
goldin-diary.oneLine: Direct on-camera flash in intimate domestic interiors.

grand-budapest-symmetrical-pastel.name: Grand Budapest symmetrical-pastel (Yeoman / Anderson)
grand-budapest-symmetrical-pastel.oneLine: Wes Anderson's *The Grand Budapest Hotel* (2014), shot by **Robert Yeoman** — Anderson's lifelong DP. The signature is **rigorous symmetrical composition** within a **pastel storybook palette** (pinks, purples, reds, blues, browns), with **three different aspect ratios deployed for three different eras**: 1.37:1 for 1930s, 2.35:1 for 1960s, 1.85:1 for 1980s. The whole film reads as a sequence of perfectly composed dollhouse vignettes.

helmut-newton-flash.name: Helmut Newton on-camera flash glamour
helmut-newton-flash.oneLine: Single hard flash on a tall confident female subject, falloff into pure black.
helmut-newton-flash.notForUseWhen: Brief is sincere, sentimental, family-friendly, or wholesome.

her-warm-pastel-future.name: Her warm-pastel near-future (van Hoytema)
her-warm-pastel-future.oneLine: Spike Jonze's *Her* (2013), shot by **Hoyte van Hoytema** on ARRI Alexa (his first feature on digital — proving warm dreamy looks don't need film). The signature is the **deliberate refusal of blue** — van Hoytema and Jonze decided against blue specifically *"to make sure it didn't seem too dystopian or foreboding."* Instead the entire film is warm-cast: pale purples, caramel browns, sage, putty, ecru, O'Keeffe reds, Rothko raspberry, creamy whites. **"A little bit of red in every frame"** was the rule.

high-key-beauty.name: High-key beauty white seamless
high-key-beauty.oneLine: Pure white seamless backdrop, even all around.

la-la-land-musical-magic.name: La La Land musical-magic (Sandgren)
la-la-land-musical-magic.oneLine: Damien Chazelle's *La La Land* (2016), shot by **Linus Sandgren** on **35mm CinemaScope (2.55:1)** — the original CinemaScope ratio used by old Hollywood musicals. The visual signature is the romantic deployment of **primary colors (red, blue, yellow) as emotional storytelling tools**, set against magic-hour LA twilight skies that lean **mercury-vapor cool** rather than the actual sodium-vapor warm of real streetlights.

leibovitz-key-light.name: Annie Leibovitz one-light portraiture
leibovitz-key-light.oneLine: Single large softbox or umbrella, ambient kept in.
leibovitz-key-light.notForUseWhen: Quick product, e-comm hero, anything needing many subjects in one shot.

magic-glow.name: Magic glow product or beauty
magic-glow.oneLine: Internal glow as if subject is lit from within.

magnum-monochrome.name: Magnum monochrome documentary
magnum-monochrome.oneLine: 35mm Leica with 35mm or 50mm lens, decisive moment.

moonlight-miami-pastel-neon.name: Moonlight Miami pastel-neon (Laxton)
moonlight-miami-pastel-neon.oneLine: Barry Jenkins' *Moonlight* (2016), shot by **James Laxton** on ARRI Alexa in **CinemaScope** — Jenkins called Liberty City a *"beautiful nightmare"* and described their move as *"paint this nightmare in beautiful tones."* The signature is the **dreamlike-but-Miami-rooted palette**: pastels (peach, lavender, mint) layered with neon (pink, purple, cyan), all bathed in tropical greens, applied to intimate close-up portraiture. Laxton shot 98% of the film himself, hand-held by his own body, to maintain proximity-as-intimacy.
moonlight-miami-pastel-neon.notForUseWhen: B2B-clean, brutalism, restrained-clean tech marketing, gritty-documentary

night-flash-noir.name: Night flash neon-noir portrait
night-flash-noir.oneLine: Hard direct on-camera flash on subject at night.

pixel-stretch-time-displacement.name: Pixel-stretch / time-displacement photo effect
pixel-stretch-time-displacement.oneLine: One row or column of pixels — typically selected from the subject's eye-line, lip-line, or strongest contour — **stretched horizontally or vertically across the entire frame**, creating a surreal smeared-motion streak. The classic Photoshop pixel-stretch technique. Used for album art (Coldplay, LCD Soundsystem-era covers), music videos, slow-burn editorial, abstract magazine spreads.

rgb-chromatic-split.name: RGB chromatic-split / channel-shift
rgb-chromatic-split.oneLine: Photo's **red, green, and blue channels separated and offset** — horizontal slide (classic CRT-fail), diagonal slide (more chaotic), or random offset (full glitch). The result: ghosted color fringes around every high-contrast edge. The classic VHS-tracking-fail / cheap-lens chromatic-aberration / 90s-music-video glitch look. Distinct from `circuit-bent-glitch` in that it's CHANNEL-SHIFT-ONLY — no datamosh, no pixel-sort, no compression noise. One technique, used with discipline.

salgado-contrast.name: Sebastião Salgado biblical contrast
salgado-contrast.oneLine: High-contrast monochrome, deep black point, retained shadow detail.

seventies-soft-grain.name: 1970s soft warm grain editorial
seventies-soft-grain.oneLine: Warm Kodachrome amber and earth tones.

shore-color.name: Stephen Shore Uncommon Places banal-color
shore-color.oneLine: 4x5 large format, deep depth of field, full edge sharpness.

sorrenti-grain.name: Mario Sorrenti grain and tonality
sorrenti-grain.oneLine: Medium format Pentax 67 or Hasselblad, 80mm normal lens.
sorrenti-grain.notForUseWhen: Anything needing color, product detail, or commercial-explicit subject.

tillmans-candid.name: Wolfgang Tillmans degree-zero candid
tillmans-candid.oneLine: One 50mm lens, no retouching, available light, point and shoot.
tillmans-candid.notForUseWhen: Luxury, glamour, conversion-focused product pages, B2B.

vaporwave-still-life.name: Vaporwave pastel still life
vaporwave-still-life.oneLine: Pastel pink and cyan dominant, soft pastel gradient backdrop.

war-photojournalism.name: Frontline war photojournalism
war-photojournalism.oneLine: 35mm or 28mm wide lens, very close to action.
war-photojournalism.notForUseWhen: Any commercial application. Reserved for editorial truth.

warm-minimal-daylight.name: Warm-minimal daylight (Kinfolk / quiet lookbook)
warm-minimal-daylight.oneLine: The shared register behind 2010s Kinfolk-magazine slow-living interiors AND post-Margiela quiet-lookbook plaster-wall exteriors. Soft natural daylight, warm muted palette, considered slow mood, generous negative space. Two sub-variants in one entry — pick by context.
warm-minimal-daylight.notForUseWhen: Tech fast-paced, edgy fashion, fast e-comm, loud kinetic brand

weingart-staged.name: Staged conceptual fine-art (Wolfgang Weingart adjacent)
weingart-staged.oneLine: Highly constructed scene, every element placed intentionally.
weingart-staged.notForUseWhen: Mass-market product, B2B SaaS, anything quick-to-decode.

y2k-flash-glam.name: Y2K glossy flash glamour
y2k-flash-glam.oneLine: Direct flash, glossy reflective fabrics, lipgloss high-shine.

y2k-halftone.name: Y2K halftone newsprint effect
y2k-halftone.oneLine: Photo passed through visible CMYK halftone dot pattern.
